text:
maria: FYI noticed a perf + quality regression after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak on mixed-quant models. throughput dropped ~18% on canary and a few structured JSON evals started failing (fields missing).
kevin: can you paste the failing eval ids and the canary job id?
maria: evals: eval-json-2026-03-17 (small prompt suite), failing on 7/120 cases — truncated/missing 'items' array. canary job id: canary-rt-9823. link to logs: https://internal.perf/redwood/canary-9823
perf-bot: Canary canary-rt-9823 deployed by @deploy-bot at 2026-03-17T22:11:04Z — changed kernel selector to try fp8-first for compatible layers.
kevin: ran lightweight profiler on canary-9823, saw more time in the attention kernels when fp8 path chosen -> seems batching/kv interaction caused extra memory copies and slower KV hits. p50 token time +20%. snippet:
```
Kernel timing (ms):
attn_fp8_forward: 0.87 -> 1.10
attn_int8_forward: 0.76
kv_cache_lookup: 0.12 -> 0.25
total per token: 1.9 -> 2.3
```
maria: interesting — the JSON breakage looks correlated with longer prefix handling. maybe KV cache stale pointers after switching kernels? got an example request with prefix length 1024 that fails reproducibly.
siva: can you run the reproducer with KV caching disabled? my hunch: the fp8 kernels changed layout/stride expectations and our cache key serialization didn't account for fallback/alternate kernel indices. quick test: set REDWOOD_KV_CACHE=off and rerun eval-json-2026-03-17 -> will report.
alisa: if disabling cache fixes quality then we should hotfix by forcing kernel-selector to preserve previous layout for cached entries while we triage. no full revert if not needed. :thinking_face:
maria: ran with KV off — throughput drops but all JSON tests pass. so cache interplay is likely.
kevin: dug into runtime stack — when we switched to fp8-first we started using a different per-layer meta (quant_variant_id) in the kernel table. cache keys currently only include model_id + layer_index + seq_end; missing quant_variant_id. so when cached KV is reused across quant variants we can get misaligned KV shapes -> silent corruption in structured output.
fernando: oof. that explains both perf and hallucination: extra copies from shape mismatch + corrupted attention state.
deploy-bot: rollback option available: revert kernel-selector change for canary-9823 (automated). do we want to rollback globally?
kevin: let's rollback canary and pause the FP8 rollout. I can make a patch to include quant_variant_id in KV cache key and add a metric to detect cache-variant-mismatch. patch: runtime: include quant_variant_id in kv_key; add guard when kv_shape != expected -> drop cached entry + inc metric kv_mismatch_count.
siva: also add a small unit test that simulates different kernel variants and ensures cache entries are isolated. I'll own that.
alisa: PR owners? kevin for patch, siva for tests, maria please run full eval suite once merged. Fernando help triage perf after patch. I'll coordinate release notes and incident blurb if rollback needed.
maria: creating ticket: https://issues.internal/RED-4821 "kv-key must include quant_variant_id — causes mixed-quant cache corruption" assigning kevin/siva.
kevin: ETA for PR and canary redeploy ~4 hours. will post updates here.
perf-bot: scheduled regression job eval-json-2026-03-17 queued to run after canary redeploy.
maria: thanks all — marking as high priority. will follow up with detailed repro and sample logs in the ticket. :thumbsup:
